notes: The Raspberry Pi model is not named. A generic 40-pin Pi with a CSI camera connector is defined as a new part type 'raspberry-pi'.
The camera ribbon cable is not in the catalogue, so a 'csi-ribbon-cable' part type was added as a connector. Its two ends are one electrical node.

Fix for the reported error: the catalogue's camera-imx219 CSI port is of kind 'edge', and no ribbon end kind is compatible with it. A wire-end and an edge were both rejected. So the ribbon-to-camera joined and electrical edges now name the ribbon's port 'a' but leave the camera port unspecified. They still record that the ribbon is plugged into the camera and carries signals to it. The ribbon's other end (port b) goes into the Pi's CSI header-socket, which is a valid pairing.
The manual's 'Pin-socket jumper leads' are matched to the catalogue's jumper-wire-mf. Port a is the female socket end on the Pi header. Port b is the male end in the breadboard.
In the diagram the black wire goes to the GND pin in the right-hand header column, which is physical pin 6. That pin is named GND.1. The orange wire goes to GP17 (GPIO17).

The diagram numbers the breadboard rows 1-13 and the columns a-e. The catalogue names holes '<column><bank>.<row>', so diagram row 3 column a is '3t.a'. The black wire ends at 3t.a and the orange wire at 5t.a.

The button is shown across diagram rows 3 and 5 on the a-e side. Its four legs are placed at 3t.c, 3t.e, 5t.c and 5t.e, which is an assumption. Side 1 (3t, GND) and side 2 (5t, GPIO17) are the two sides of the button.
The button has no external pull resistor. The code uses gpiozero Button(17), which enables the Pi's internal pull-up, and the other side of the button goes to GND.
Software steps such as the Python code, rpicam-hello and ffmpeg are not hardware parts. The USB power cable and the monitor/keyboard are not modelled.
The breadboard and jumper leads were listed as 'None' in the parts match, but equivalent catalogue types (breadboard, jumper-wire-mf) were used.
